transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Sofia Patel (Redwood AE), Marco Chen (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Dr. Aaron Banks (CTO, Zenith), Maya Singh (Platform Lead), Jamal Reed (Security Architect), Priya Kapoor (Data Engineer)

[00:00] Sofia: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, uh, happy to kick this off. I'm Sofia from Redwood, i'm the AE on the account. Marco and Lena are with me, Marco will run the technical bits.
[00:12] Dr. Aaron: Hey Sofia, thanks. I'm Aaron, this is Maya, Jamal and Priya. Excited to get started.
[00:17] Marco: quick intro from my side, i'm Marco Chen, solutions engineer. We'll want to cover the private deployment options and what telemetry we need for the pilot.
[00:27] Lena: and i'll own the onboarding project and timeline. We'll put together milestones and check-ins.
[00:33] Sofia: Great. Agenda — 1) confirm success criteria and timeline, 2) security/compliance requirements, 3) deployment options, 4) pilot scope and next steps. Does that look right?
[00:42] Maya: Yep that works. Our primary constraints: data residency (we need EU-only processing), SSO with SAML, and strong KMS integration. Latency targets are 300ms p95 for patient-facing features, and cost is also a consideration.
[00:58] Marco: ok got it. quick clarification — when you say 300ms p95, is that token latency or end-to-end API?
[01:05] Maya: end-to-end for short prompts, about 250-400 tokens.
[01:10] Marco: good, that helps. For data residency and SSO we typically recommend Redwood Private in a VPC — gives you control, KMS integration and SAML SSO via your IdP. Dedicated can work if you want isolation but still use our control plane, hosted won't meet data residency unless we provision a region.
[01:28] Jamal: can you run through the difference between Private and Dedicated again? We've seen those terms mixed.
[01:33] Marco: yes, quick one — Dedicated is reserved capacity on our hosted infra: predictable throughput and tenant isolation, but metadata and control plane still in Redwood cloud. Private is customer-managed networking and the control plane is in your VPC or on-prem; you manage keys and networking. So for EU-only processing + KMS, Private is the safer choice.
[01:53] Dr. Aaron: ok that leans Private. What's the typical uplift on cost and what about operational burden?
[02:00] Sofia: cost uplift depends on commit size and infra choices. There's a platform fee for Private plus infra ops. We can model it in the pricing sheet — i'll share an initial estimate. For ops, we provide an installer and a managed control plane option where we still help with upgrades.
[02:15] Priya: do you support HSM or BYOK? Our KMS has an HSM-backed key policy.
[02:21] Marco: yes we support KMS and HSM integrations; BYOK is supported in Private. There can be some network setup for key access if you want the HSM inside your VPC.
[02:31] Jamal: audit logs — do you ship logs to our SIEM or we pull them?
[02:36] Lena: we can push audit logs to your S3 or to your SIEM via connector, and we keep a separate retention option. We'll share retention SLAs in the doc.
[02:44] Maya: another question, model catalog — we have a preference for open models and quantized variants. Will we be able to pin model versions?
[02:52] Marco: yes, you can pin versions and we support quantized models for lower-cost inference. For very low-latency you can pick smaller model variants or use batching/caching knobs. Our runtime supports KV cache but sometimes transcription or notes show it as K V cash, you might see weird transcriptions.
[03:10] Dr. Aaron: (laughs) noted. For the pilot — what does a typical pilot look like?
[03:16] Sofia: usually 4 weeks: week 0 internal alignment and infra prep, week 1 deploy in Private sandbox and smoke tests, week 2 run benchmarks with sample traffic, week 3 quality checks and tuning, then a rollout plan. We'll do a canary and then expand.
[03:33] Maya: timeline wise we want pilot start roughly in mid-October. Is that doable?
[03:38] Marco: yes mid-October is feasible. We'll need your network contacts and some sample workload in by the end of September.
[03:45] Priya: we can provide sample traffic and anonymized logs. How much data is helpful?
[03:50] Marco: a week's worth of representative requests is helpful — request sizes and percent of chats needing long context. Also, token distributions. That lets us pick kernel/quant settings.
[04:02] Jamal: security questionnaire — we'll send the full vendor security form. Can you do a response turn-around?
[04:08] Sofia: yes typical turnaround is 3-5 business days for the standard questionnaire, for custom items we may need the security team, but we'll push it.
[04:15] Jamal: fine. Also need contract language around data ownership and e-discovery.
[04:20] Sofia: we'll share standard clauses and highlight Private deployment options that keep data in your control. Legal can sync after this call.
[04:27] Dr. Aaron: ok. On monitoring — we need token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency metrics.
[04:33] Lena: Redwood Console includes token-level cost & latency, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. We'll include sample screenshots in the onboarding pack.
[04:41] Maya: what about canary / rollout control? We might want A/B test models.
[04:45] Marco: rollouts support canary, A/B, and automatic fallback policies. We'll show you the UI and API during the technical deep-dive.
[04:55] Dr. Aaron: any recommended quantization settings for medical text? We care about accuracy.
[05:00] Marco: for clinical content i'd start with 8-bit quantization and run quality evals on your prompt set; Redwood Optimize will give model/quant recommendation based on the eval results. We avoid extreme quant that causes hallucinations.
[05:14] Priya: is there a sandbox or dev cluster we can hit before we spin up the Private?
[05:19] Sofia: yes we can provide a hosted sandbox with an isolated API key for integration testing while the Private infra is provisioned. That helps integrate SSO and initial calls.
[05:29] Maya: network questions — do you support cross-account VPC peering and transit gateway?
[05:33] Marco: yes both patterns. We'll prepare a network diagram with peering and transit gateway options. For EU region, we have partners and can do a region-specific deployment.
[05:45] Jamal: encryption in transit — mTLS?
[05:48] Marco: yes mTLS supported and mutual auth for internal components; we can show cert rotation steps.
[05:54] Dr. Aaron: ok great. Let's talk success criteria — what do you need from us to call pilot successful?
[06:01] Sofia: typically 1) performance: meet your 300ms p95 for the test profile, 2) quality: maintain accuracy thresholds on eval prompts, 3) security: pass your vendor security checklist and KMS integration, 4) operational: runbook and monitoring validated.
[06:17] Maya: sounds good. We'll confirm the exact thresholds and give you an eval set.
[06:21] Sofia: perfect. Next — are there any blockers?
[06:24] Priya: network approvals may take a week; also legal needs to review privacy addendum.
[06:29] Lena: we'll put those dependencies on the timeline and follow up with contacts.
[06:33] Sofia: ok, i'll send the onboarding checklist after the call. Marco will schedule a technical deep-dive — that will cover VPC peering, installer steps, and perf benchmarks.
[06:44] Marco: for the deep-dive i'll want to run through your sample traffic and maybe do a quick perf run in our hosted sandbox to get rough numbers.
[06:52] Dr. Aaron: are you able to share any previous benchmark numbers for similar workloads, maybe healthcare customers?
[06:58] Marco: we have anonymized benchmarks; i'll share a short benchmark pack. We also publish model profiles — but we'll tailor the numbers after we see your traffic.
[07:08] Maya: any compliance certs you can share? SOC 2 Type II?
[07:12] Sofia: yes SOC 2 Type II report available under NDA; we'll include the summary and next steps to request full report.
[07:20] Jamal: can we get the data flow diagram early? It's helpful for our security review.
[07:24] Marco: yes we'll include a draft data flow diagram and network diagram in the packet.
[07:28] Priya: can Redwood integrate with our existing logging pipeline (Splunk)?
[07:32] Lena: yes we have connectors and can push logs to S3, Splunk HEC, or other endpoints.
[07:37] Sofia: recap — i'll share onboarding checklist, pricing estimate, SOC 2 summary and the sandbox API keys. Marco will share network diagram, benchmark pack, and schedule a technical deep-dive the week of Sep 21. Lena will create the onboarding project and invite your team. Jamal & Priya will provide the security questionnaire and sample traffic by Sep 20.
[07:58] Dr. Aaron: sounds good. One more quick thing — support SLAs during pilot? We need a point of contact.
[08:04] Lena: you'll have a CSM and an SE on-call; for Private we offer premium support add-on if needed.
[08:11] Sofia: we'll include contact details in the packet.
[08:14] Maya: ok, thanks everyone.
[08:16] Sofia: thanks all. we'll follow up with the packet and calendar invites.
[08:20] (meeting ends)

Notes about transcription: occasional minor mistranscriptions (e.g., K V cache vs KV cache) and some speaker overlap.
